notes: Held-out perplexity rests heavily on the unresolved-step policy: 33% of scored outcomes fell off the model entirely and took the uniform fallback. It is NOT a like-for-like comparison against the training figure.
Repeat/exact-match section recomputed from stored cells after a fix to artifact filename keying; the run itself was not repeated.

edge_bases.edges_simple_no_loops: distinct (tail, head) pairs where tail != head
edge_bases.edges_total: every edge line, multi-edges preserved, self-loops included

formulas.branching_factor: edges_total / nodes  (paper definition; edge basis = multi-edges PRESERVED, self-loops included. NOTE: this is not the conventional mean out-degree)
formulas.density: edges_simple_no_loops / (nodes * (nodes - 1))  (textbook directed simple-graph density, retained for comparability with the wider graph literature but NOT the headline density -- see reachability_density for why. Multi-edges COLLAPSED and self-loops EXCLUDED from the numerator, because V*(V-1) counts ordered distinct pairs and neither is representable in it; leaving them in can push density above 1. Null when nodes < 2.)
formulas.path_linearity: longest_path_edges / edges_total  (longest path measured in EDGES traversed, over the same preserved edge basis)
formulas.reachability_density: |{(u,v) : u != v, v reachable from u}| / (nodes * (nodes - 1))  (HEADLINE density. The paper gives no formula, defining density only by intent -- it "captures how easily an attacker can traverse the network". This is the literal reading: the fraction of ordered state pairs the attacker can actually get between, following edges any distance. Same normalisation as edge density, so it stays in [0,1] and remains comparable across graphs. Preferred over edge density because edge density is confounded by graph size -- measured across the 104 CPTC-2017 baseline AGs, corr(nodes, edge_density) = -0.79 versus corr(nodes, reachability_density) = +0.17 -- and because the paper already defines branching_factor = edges/nodes, which an edges-per-node density largely duplicates. Null when nodes < 2.)
formulas.simplicity: nodes / edges_total  (reciprocal of branching_factor; same edge basis. Included only for comparability with Nadeem et al.)

formulas.raw_alerts_per_ag: raw_alerts / n_attack_graphs  (the same ratio over alerts SAGE actually ingests, i.e. after the event_type and dataset filters. Diverges sharply from the primary on CPTC-2018, where the bad-IP filter drops ~69% of records.)
formulas.raw_records_per_ag: raw_records / n_attack_graphs  (PRIMARY -- the paper defines compression as "number of raw alerts divided by number of generated attack graphs", and its own dataset counts pin "raw alerts" to every record in the file: it cites CCDC-2018 as 1,052,281, which is exactly the raw_records count here, whereas the post-filter alert count is 1,033,067. See RAW_ALERT_CONVENTION.)

compression.raw_alert_convention: raw_records: every JSON object in the dataset files. Matches the paper convention, confirmed exactly against its CCDC-2018 count of 1,052,281.

heldout.formula: PP = exp( -(1/N) * sum_i log P(outcome_i | state_i) ), N = total scored outcomes. Outcomes at a state are the alphabet symbols plus an explicit END event, so N counts one END per trace in addition to every symbol.
heldout.note: Held-out: a second FlexFringe run on the training split only. Not comparable to the training perplexity, and never averaged with it.
heldout.oov_policy: union_alphabet: n_outcomes spans the union of the training and scored alphabets plus END, so an unseen symbol receives alpha / (N_state + alpha * n_outcomes) rather than zero. Counted in oov_events.
heldout.prob_formula: P(sym|state)  = (trans_counts[sym] + alpha) / (N_state + alpha * n_outcomes) ; P(END|state)  = (total_final   + alpha) / (N_state + alpha * n_outcomes) ; N_state = total_paths + total_final ; n_outcomes = |alphabet| + 1
heldout.unresolved_policy: uniform_over_outcomes: an unresolvable step (traverse state -1) is scored as 1/n_outcomes rather than skipped, and counted in unresolved_events

training.formula: PP = exp( -(1/N) * sum_i log P(outcome_i | state_i) ), N = total scored outcomes. Outcomes at a state are the alphabet symbols plus an explicit END event, so N counts one END per trace in addition to every symbol.
